messages:
sanjay: Heads-up - saw a 1.8-2x tail latency regression on SM92 nodes for seqlen=64 after yesterday's kernel routing tweak. Repro on perf farm.

olivia: ouch. can you paste numbers + which commit? :eyes:

sanjay: commit 0f3a9b5 changed kernel ordering for small sequences (prefer new fp8-tc path). Perf microbench (64 tokens, batch=8):
```
before: p50 45ms p95 72ms p99 90ms
after:  p50 46ms p95 125ms p99 170ms
```
Not consistent across machines - only SM92 fleet.

kevin: do we have a capdetect misreport? TC/FP8 detection sometimes lies with this driver combo. which driver on the bad hosts?

sanjay: driver 540.2 on bad hosts; some SM92 nodes report TC supported but microbench shows fallback to generic kernel. nv-nsight dump shows kernel name `matmul_fallback_f32` instead of `matmul_tc_fp8`.

maria: pasted a short nsight stacktrace:
```
Kernel: matmul_fallback_f32
SM: 92
Driver: 540.2
Occupancy: 32% (expected ~70% for tc path)
Duration: 1.2ms per chunk (~2x)
```
probable cause: we route to tc path by capability flags but at runtime kernel launch fails fast and falls back. that fallback path is heavier for seqlen=64 because it disables our microbatching fastpath.

olivia: hmm KV cache behavior could exacerbate this if we evict and rewarm repeatedly at that seqlen boundary. did you see KV churn?

sanjay: yes - saw repeated KV invalidations when >1 requester hits mixed-length sequences. sample log: `kvcache: evict prefix mismatch seqlen boundary 64->128` happening every 700ms.

kevin: two coupled issues then: (1) capability detection allowing an optimistic TC/FP8 route, (2) our runtime fallback to generic kernel causing microbatching mismatch and KV churn. want to try making capdetect stricter + add hysteresis on kernel path selection.

maria: can we require a small on-device micro-run as part of capdetect? e.g. run a tiny GEMM with fp8 path and check result/latency before committing?

kevin: +1. proposed patch: reorder capdetect: 1) check SM >= 92, 2) driver >= 540, 3) attempt `tc_fp8_probe()` (fast micro-run, <=1ms), 4) only flip capability flag if probe passes. Also add `cap_hysteresis_ms=300000` so we don't flip back/forth quickly.

olivia: sounds good. also add a seqlen-hysteresis: once kernel path chosen for a request, keep path for next N requests or M ms when seqlen close to boundary (e.g., 56-72). avoids KV thrash.

sanjay: here's a tiny probe we ran:
```
// C-like pseudo
int tc_fp8_probe() {
  launch(tc_gemm_probe, smallA, smallB);
  sync();
  if (memcmp(result, ref, 16) == 0 && elapsed < 1.5ms) return 0; // ok
  return -1; // fallback
}
```
on bad host this returns -1 despite SM92 flags.

perfbot: CI perf-regression job 4920 failed: seqlen=64 p95 increased by 72% on test-sm92. https://ci.internal/runs/4920

maria: i'll queue a canary build with kevin's capdetect reorder + seqlen hysteresis flags on the dedicated SM92 pool. will attach telemetry (kernel_choice, probe_result, kvcache_evictions).

kevin: add a feature flag `runtime.strict_probe=true` + `runtime.seqlen_hysteresis_ms=5000` for canary. if canary looks good, roll to prod via canary->gradual.

olivia: also add a test to perf suite: synthetic mixed-length workload (seq=32/64/128 random) with high concurrency to check KV eviction rate and p95. must fail build if kv_evictions_per_min > X or p95 regresses > 10%.

sanjay: i'll collect nsight traces + a short repro script and upload to the perf bucket. link incoming.

maria: launched canary at 10:14 UTC on SM92-dedicated-3 pool. initial telemetry: kernel_choice=tc_fp8_probe_failed for 6/8 hosts, kvcache_evictions dropped 70% after hysteresis applied, p95 back to ~baseline. will run longer.

kevin: great. if those numbers hold, we keep strict_probe default for SM92 and put a short rollback window. i'll open a PR with tests + docs. target: patch + canary validation in 48h.

olivia: thanks all. please post CI links and the repro script once uploaded. :thumbsup:
